controls.description: Bank reconciliations are prepared promptly each month and reviewed and signed off by a person independent of cash handling, who investigates aged or unusual items.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Signed reconciliations with review notes and documented follow-up of outstanding items.
controls.limitations: Review may be superficial; will not detect items omitted from both the bank statement and the books.
controls.objective: Ensure bank errors and irregularities are detected and investigated promptly.
controls.responsible_role: Finance manager, independent of cash handling
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Aged outstanding items (unpresented cheques, deposits in transit) are investigated and cleared or written back within a defined timeframe.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Aged items listing with investigation notes and resolution.
controls.limitations: Depends on the reviewer genuinely investigating rather than carrying items forward.
controls.objective: Prevent stale items from permanently distorting the reported cash balance.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: New beneficiaries are independently verified (business existence, bank account ownership) before the first payment is made.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Beneficiary verification checklist with supporting documents.
controls.limitations: Verification documents can be forged; does not prevent subsequent diversion of payments to changed bank details.
controls.objective: Prevent payments to fictitious or improper beneficiaries.
controls.responsible_role: Finance / procurement, independent of payment processing
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Payments above defined thresholds require dual authorisation, and supporting documents are matched to the payment before release.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Authorised payment batches with matched supporting documents.
controls.limitations: Can be overridden by management; authorisers may approve without examining supporting documents.
controls.objective: Ensure only genuine, properly supported payments are released.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: All transfers between the entity's bank accounts are logged in a transfer register and matched on both the sending and receiving sides before period-end close.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Transfer register with both-side matching evidence and sign-off.
controls.limitations: Will not detect transfers deliberately excluded from the register; depends on completeness of the log.
controls.objective: Ensure inter-account transfers are completely and accurately recorded on both sides.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Year-end bank cut-off procedures require transfers in transit at the reporting date to be identified, listed and correctly presented (not double-counted).
controls.evidence_of_operation: Year-end in-transit schedule agreed to bank statements on both sides.
controls.limitations: Only as complete as the transfer register and the statements obtained; post year-end reversals may not be visible.
controls.objective: Prevent cut-off errors and window dressing through year-end transfers.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Independent surprise cash counts are performed, reconciled to the cash records, and differences investigated and approved.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Count sheets signed by the counter, reconciliation to records, investigation of differences.
controls.limitations: Only proves the position at the count date; ineffective if the counter colludes with the cashier.
controls.objective: Detect shortages or misappropriation of cash on hand.
controls.responsible_role: Finance / internal audit, independent of cash custody
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Cash on hand is held under dual custody, all receipts are issued pre-numbered receipts, and takings are banked promptly and intact.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Receipt books, banking slips, dual-control logs.
controls.limitations: Dual custody can be defeated by collusion; does not prevent theft before receipting.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorised removal of physical cash.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Bank statements or confirmations that disagree with the reconciled balance.
evidence.description: The entity's reconciliation of the cash book balance to the bank statement balance, listing outstanding items.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Prepared promptly after month-end; outstanding items listed with dates; preparer and reviewer identified.
evidence.limitations: Internally prepared; proves arithmetic agreement, not that outstanding items are genuine.
evidence.name: Bank reconciliation
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on independent review and investigation of outstanding items. An unreviewed reconciliation is the record under test, not corroboration of the cash balance.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Bank-originated transactions with no corresponding book entry.
evidence.description: The bank-issued statement of account transactions and balances for the period.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Original or bank-portal download; covering the full period including cut-off dates.
evidence.limitations: Shows bank movements only; does not explain their business purpose.
evidence.name: Bank statement
evidence.reliability_notes: Obtained directly from the bank it is strong independent evidence of movements and balances; a client-provided copy is less reliable and should be agreed to the confirmation where risk is high.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Reconciliation balances that differ from the confirmed balance.
evidence.description: Direct written confirmation from the bank of account balances, facilities and related matters at the reporting date, obtained by the auditor.
evidence.expected_characteristics: On bank letterhead or secure electronic format; addressed to the auditor; covering all accounts.
evidence.limitations: Confirms balances at a point in time only; does not address transactions during the period.
evidence.name: Bank confirmation letter
evidence.reliability_notes: High reliability: obtained directly by the auditor from an independent third party, specifically for the audit purpose.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Outstanding items that remain uncleared long after the reporting date.
evidence.description: Schedule of unpresented cheques, deposits in transit and other reconciling items with dates and amounts.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Aged analysis; each item dated; explanations for aged items.
evidence.limitations: A schedule proves items were listed, not that they are genuine.
evidence.name: Outstanding items schedule
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability comes from vouching items to subsequent bank statements and supporting documents; an aged, uninvestigated schedule is itself an indicator of weak controls.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Payments with no entry in the payment register (off-book payments).
evidence.description: The complete listing of payments made in the period, showing date, beneficiary, amount and supporting reference.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete and sequential; reconcilable to bank outflows.
evidence.limitations: Only records payments entered into the system; payments made outside the system leave no trace here.
evidence.name: Payment register / bank payment listing
evidence.reliability_notes: System-generated listings are more reliable than manual ones. The register is the population under test for unusual payments, not corroboration of their validity.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Supporting documents that are inconsistent, photocopied without originals, or contradicted by third-party evidence.
evidence.description: Invoices, contracts, purchase orders, expense claims or other documents presented as support for a payment.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Original or verifiable; consistent dates, amounts and beneficiary details; approved where applicable.
evidence.limitations: Documents can be fabricated; inspection assesses consistency, not authenticity, unless corroborated externally.
evidence.name: Supporting documents for payments
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability increases where documents are originals, independently approved, and corroborated to third-party evidence (e.g. supplier statements). A document alone does not prove the underlying transaction was genuine.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Beneficiaries paid with no verification record on file.
evidence.description: Records of the checks performed before adding a beneficiary: business registration, bank account verification, and approval.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Dated before the first payment; verifier independent of payment processing; supporting documents retained.
evidence.limitations: Verification is a point-in-time check; bank details may be changed afterwards.
evidence.name: Beneficiary verification records
evidence.reliability_notes: More reliable where verification used independent sources (e.g. direct bank confirmation of account ownership) rather than documents supplied by the beneficiary.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Transfers recorded on one side only at the reporting date.
evidence.description: Log of transfers between the entity's bank accounts, showing date, amount, sending and receiving accounts.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete for the period; both sides identifiable; sequential or dated.
evidence.limitations: Only complete if all transfers are logged; deliberate omissions leave no trace.
evidence.name: Inter-account transfer register
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on completeness of logging; corroboration comes from matching both sides to bank statements.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Transfer advices that do not agree with the bank statements.
evidence.description: Bank-issued advices or system confirmations for individual transfers around the reporting date.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Bank-generated; showing value date, amount, and sending/receiving accounts.
evidence.limitations: Proves the transfer instruction, not that both sides were recorded correctly.
evidence.name: Bank transfer advices
evidence.reliability_notes: Bank-generated advices are independent evidence of the transfer; value dates are key for cut-off testing.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Cash records exceeding the counted cash.
evidence.description: The entity's record of a cash count: denominations counted, total, counter identity and date.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Denomination breakdown; signed by an independent counter; dated.
evidence.limitations: Proves the count was recorded, not that it was performed properly or independently.
evidence.name: Cash count sheets
evidence.reliability_notes: More reliable where the count was surprise and the counter independent of custody; weakened where the cashier counted their own cash.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Petty cash vouchers without receipts or approval.
evidence.description: Petty cash book, vouchers and receipts recording cash held and disbursed.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Vouchers supported by receipts; approved; balanced to the float.
evidence.limitations: Internally maintained; IOUs or unsupported vouchers may be included as cash.
evidence.name: Petty cash records and vouchers
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on independent review and the discipline of supporting every disbursement with a receipt; IOUs recorded as cash overstate the balance.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Entity count sheets showing a different total for the same cash.
evidence.description: The auditor's independent record of cash counted, by denomination, at the time of the count.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Recorded independently at the time; denominations stated; witnessed where appropriate.
evidence.limitations: Covers only the cash presented for counting; concealed cash is outside its scope.
evidence.name: Auditor's cash count record
evidence.reliability_notes: High reliability for existence of the cash counted: obtained directly by the auditor through inspection.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether bank balances are material; how often reconciliations are prepared and by whom; whether any independent review exists; the age profile of outstanding items.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where bank balances are material. Less applicable where the owner reviews the bank statements personally each month, or where balances are trivial - though unreviewed reconciliations remain a deficiency, the risk of material misstatement is then low.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: the bank reconciliation is the key control over cash, and its independent review is a standard expectation.
factor_risk.explanation: The bank reconciliation is the primary detective control over cash: it is where unrecorded bank transactions, errors and irregularities surface. Without independent review, the preparer - who may also handle cash - can conceal differences, and genuine errors go unchallenged. This is a control deficiency creating detection risk, not evidence of misstatement.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Bank reconciliations are prepared without independent review, or are not prepared regularly, and bank balances are material.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: The volume and value of payments to new or unfamiliar beneficiaries; how new beneficiaries are verified; payment approval thresholds and whether they are enforced; who can add beneficiaries to the payment system.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where payments are processed in volume or by electronic file. Less applicable where every payment is individually reviewed and authorised by the owner with full knowledge of the business's suppliers - the opportunity for an unfamiliar beneficiary to pass unnoticed is then minimal.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: payments to unknown beneficiaries are a standard fraud indicator tested through vouching and beneficiary analysis.
factor_risk.explanation: Payments to unfamiliar beneficiaries bypass the implicit control of a known supplier relationship: there is no purchase history, no expected pattern, and often no independent party who would notice the payment is wrong. Combined with weak beneficiary verification, this creates the opportunity to divert funds to fictitious or improper recipients. The payments are indicators to investigate, not proof of fraud.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Payments are made to beneficiaries that are not recognised suppliers or employees, and new beneficiaries are not independently verified before payment.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: The value and timing of transfers around the reporting date; whether a transfer register is maintained; whether both sides of each transfer are recorded in the same period; whether transfers are reversed after year-end.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where transfers around the reporting date are material. Less applicable where the entity operates a single bank account, or where transfers are automatically swept with same-day value on both sides - the cut-off exposure is then minimal.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: year-end bank transfer cut-off testing is a standard procedure addressing double-counting and window dressing.
factor_risk.explanation: A transfer debited from one account but not yet credited to the other at the reporting date sits in transit. If recorded as received before it arrives, the same cash is counted twice; if omitted on both sides, cash is understated. Around year-end this timing difference can also be used deliberately to inflate the reported cash position. The factor creates cut-off risk that must be tested on both sides of each transfer.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Material transfers between the entity's bank accounts occur in the days immediately before or after the reporting date.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether cash on hand is material; where cash is held and by whom; whether any independent counts are performed; the volume of cash transactions.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where cash on hand is material or cash transactions are significant. Less applicable where the business is fully banked with trivial petty cash - the assertion risk is then immaterial even though the control point stands.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: physical verification of cash is the direct test of existence for cash on hand.
factor_risk.explanation: Cash is the most portable asset and the easiest to misappropriate without trace. Without independent physical verification, shortages accumulate undetected and the recorded balance drifts from reality. The factor indicates that existence must be tested directly; it does not prove any shortage exists.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Cash on hand is material or cash transactions are significant, and cash is not independently counted and reconciled to records.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where bank balances are material and reconciliations are the primary control over cash. Relevant whether reconciliations are missing, late, or prepared but never reviewed.
factors.description: Bank reconciliations are prepared but no independent person reviews them, or reconciliations are not prepared regularly, so errors and irregularities in bank transactions go undetected.
factors.name: Bank reconciliations are not independently reviewed
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Stale outstanding items carried for months; reconciliations prepared long after month-end; reconciling items without explanation; the preparer also handles cash receipts or payments.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where payments are processed in volume or by electronic file, and where new beneficiaries can be added without independent verification.
factors.description: Payments are made to beneficiaries that are not recognised suppliers or employees - including new payees, one-off recipients or round-sum transfers - without adequate scrutiny.
factors.name: Unusual payments are made to unfamiliar beneficiaries
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Payments to new beneficiaries with no purchase history; round-sum payments; payments just below approval thresholds; beneficiary names similar to known suppliers; payments to individuals rather than businesses.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where the entity operates multiple bank accounts and transfers between them around the reporting date are material.
factors.description: Material transfers between the entity's bank accounts occur in the days immediately before and after the reporting date.
factors.name: Bank transfers occur around year-end
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Large transfers on the last working day; transfers recorded on one side but not the other at year-end; in-transit items inflating cash; transfers reversed shortly after year-end.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where cash on hand (tills, petty cash, undeposited receipts) is material or cash transactions are significant.
factors.description: Cash on hand (petty cash, tills, undeposited receipts) is not counted independently or reconciled to records, so shortages go undetected.
factors.name: Cash balances are not physically verified where appropriate
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Petty cash never counted; IOUs held in the cash box; the cashier also keeps the cash records; frequent small shortages written off without investigation.

procedure_evidence.notes: Reconciliations are the documents inspected.
Reconciliation is reperformed.
Bank statement is the independent source agreed to.
Outstanding items are the population vouched.
Subsequent statements corroborate clearance.
Confirmation is obtained and agreed to the reconciled balance.
Payment register is the population sampled.
Supporting documents are vouched to.
Payment data is analysed by beneficiary.
Verification records corroborate beneficiary legitimacy.
Verification records are traced to for new beneficiaries.
New beneficiaries are extracted from the payment data.
Payment batches are inspected for approval evidence.
Supporting documents are checked as matched.
Transfer register provides the population of year-end transfers.
Both sides are matched to bank statements.
Advices corroborate value dates and amounts.
In-transit schedule is reperformed from the register.
Both sides are agreed to bank statements.
Auditor's count record is the primary output.
Entity count sheets are compared where they exist.
Count sheets are reconciled.
Petty cash records are the other side of the reconciliation.
The count observed is the evidence inspected.

procedures.exception_criteria: Reconciliations unsigned or reviewed by the preparer; long-outstanding items carried without investigation; reconciliations prepared months late.
procedures.expected_result: Reconciliations are prepared promptly and show evidence of independent review, with aged items investigated.
procedures.follow_up: Review failures are control deficiencies, not proof of misstatement. Assess the deficiency and expand substantive procedures over the bank balance and outstanding items.
procedures.objective: Determine whether the bank reconciliation control operates as designed.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across months, always including the year-end reconciliation.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of monthly bank reconciliations, including year-end.
Inspect each for evidence of preparation date, independent reviewer sign-off, and follow-up of outstanding items.
Note reconciliations prepared late, reviewed by the preparer, or carrying aged unexplained items.
procedures.title: Inspect bank reconciliations for independent review

procedures.exception_criteria: Reperformance differs from the client's reconciliation; reconciling items unsupported or misdated.
procedures.expected_result: The reperformance agrees with the client's reconciliation; reconciling items are valid and correctly dated.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate differences; quantify the effect on the reported cash balance; if the reconciliation does not reconcile, treat the cash balance as uncorroborated and extend procedures.
procedures.objective: Independently verify the year-end bank reconciliation.
procedures.population: Year-end bank reconciliation and supporting records.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the year-end bank reconciliation, the cash book and the bank statement.
Independently reperform the reconciliation: agree the cash book and bank statement balances, and re-list outstanding items.
Verify each reconciling item is valid and dated correctly.
procedures.title: Reperform the year-end bank reconciliation

procedures.exception_criteria: Outstanding items that never clear; deposits in transit with no subsequent receipt; cheques outstanding for months.
procedures.expected_result: Each material outstanding item clears shortly after the reporting date or is validly explained.
procedures.follow_up: For items that do not clear, investigate with management; consider whether the cash balance is overstated and propose adjustment; stale items may indicate the reconciliation is being used to conceal differences.
procedures.objective: Verify that outstanding items in the bank reconciliation are genuine.
procedures.population: Outstanding items at the reporting date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of material and aged items; sample of routine recent items.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the aged outstanding items schedule at the reporting date.
Trace each material and aged item to the subsequent bank statement to confirm clearance.
For items not cleared, inspect supporting documents and obtain explanations.
procedures.title: Vouch aged outstanding items to subsequent clearance

procedures.exception_criteria: Confirmed balance differs from the reconciled balance; confirmation reveals accounts not in the books.
procedures.expected_result: The confirmed balance agrees with the reconciled bank balance; all accounts are captured.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate differences; unrecorded accounts or facilities may indicate completeness issues or undisclosed borrowings.
procedures.objective: Obtain independent confirmation of bank balances at the reporting date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of bank accounts, including closed accounts.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Prepare bank confirmation requests for all accounts, controlled by the auditor throughout.
Send requests directly to the banks and receive responses directly.
Agree confirmed balances to the bank reconciliations and investigate differences.
procedures.title: Obtain direct bank confirmation of balances

procedures.exception_criteria: Payments with no supporting documents; documents inconsistent with the payment (wrong beneficiary, altered amounts); payments with no business purpose.
procedures.expected_result: Each sampled payment is supported by valid documentation consistent with the beneficiary, amount and business purpose.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate each unsupported payment with management; trace the funds where possible; quantify improper payments; evaluate fraud risk indicators without presuming fraud.
procedures.objective: Verify that unusual payments to unfamiliar beneficiaries are genuine and properly supported.
procedures.population: Payments to new or unfamiliar beneficiaries in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Risk-based sample: all large or round-sum payments to new beneficiaries; sample of smaller ones.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Extract payments to new or unfamiliar beneficiaries from the payment register.
For a sample, vouch each payment to supporting documents: invoice or contract, approval, and evidence of goods or services received.
Verify the beneficiary's details against the verification records and the bank instruction.
procedures.title: Vouch unusual payments to supporting documentation

procedures.exception_criteria: Beneficiaries appearing suddenly with large payments; round-sum payments; payments just below approval thresholds; duplicate beneficiary names with different bank details.
procedures.expected_result: Payment patterns are consistent with the business's known suppliers and operations; anomalies are explained.
procedures.follow_up: Vouch anomalies to supporting documentation and beneficiary verification records; investigate with management.
procedures.objective: Identify anomalous payment patterns indicative of improper beneficiaries.
procedures.population: Full payment register for the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Full-population scan; targeted follow-up of exceptions.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Analyse payments by beneficiary: new beneficiaries, payment frequency, round sums, and amounts relative to approval thresholds.
Compare beneficiary names and bank details for near-duplicates.
Investigate anomalies against purchase history and business operations.
procedures.title: Analyse payments by beneficiary for anomalies

procedures.exception_criteria: New beneficiaries paid with no verification record; verification performed after the first payment.
procedures.expected_result: Each new beneficiary paid in the period was independently verified before the first payment.
procedures.follow_up: For unverified beneficiaries, perform full vouching of their payments; assess the control deficiency.
procedures.objective: Verify that new beneficiaries are subject to independent verification before payment.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample of new beneficiaries, weighted toward the largest first payments.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the list of beneficiaries added in the period.
For a sample, trace each to the beneficiary verification record and supporting documents.
Confirm verification predates the first payment.
procedures.title: Trace new beneficiaries to verification evidence

procedures.exception_criteria: Payments released without required authorisation; single authorisation where dual is required; supporting documents not matched.
procedures.expected_result: Payments show the required authorisations with supporting documents matched before release.
procedures.follow_up: Authorisation failures are control deficiencies, not proof payments were improper. Increase substantive vouching of payments released without proper authorisation.
procedures.objective: Test whether payment authorisation controls operate as designed.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across the period, including large and unusual payments.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of payment batches.
Inspect each for the required authorisations (including dual authorisation above thresholds).
Verify supporting documents were matched to the payment before release.
procedures.title: Test payment authorisation controls

procedures.exception_criteria: Transfers recorded as received before the value date; transfers recorded on one side only at year-end; in-transit amounts included in cash without disclosure of the double-count.
procedures.expected_result: Each year-end transfer is recorded in the correct period on both sides; in-transit amounts are correctly presented.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify cut-off errors and propose adjustments; if transfers were used to inflate cash deliberately, reassess fraud risk and consider the implications for the audit.
procedures.objective: Verify that inter-account transfers around year-end are recorded in the correct period on both sides.
procedures.population: All inter-account transfers in the cut-off window around the reporting date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of material transfers in the cut-off window.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the transfer register and bank statements for all accounts for the cut-off window.
For each transfer, match the debit on the sending account to the credit on the receiving account, noting value dates.
Verify each side is recorded in the correct period and that in-transit amounts are not double-counted.
procedures.title: Match both sides of year-end transfers

procedures.exception_criteria: Advices missing for recorded transfers; value dates inconsistent with recording; transfers reversed shortly after year-end without explanation.
procedures.expected_result: Transfer advices support the recorded transfers, with value dates consistent with the period of recording.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate missing or inconsistent advices; post year-end reversals may indicate window dressing and require reassessment of the cash position.
procedures.objective: Corroborate recorded year-end transfers to bank-issued evidence.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of material transfers in the cut-off window.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain bank transfer advices for material transfers around the reporting date.
Agree amount, accounts and value dates to the transfer register and bank statements.
Note transfers reversed shortly after year-end and obtain explanations.
procedures.title: Inspect transfer advices and bank statements

procedures.exception_criteria: In-transit schedule that does not reconcile; in-transit amounts included in the cash balance twice.
procedures.expected_result: The in-transit schedule reconciles: amounts in transit at year-end are identified once and correctly presented.
procedures.follow_up: Propose adjustments for double-counted or omitted amounts; if material, evaluate the effect on the audit opinion.
procedures.objective: Verify the completeness and accuracy of the year-end in-transit position.
procedures.population: In-transit items at the reporting date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of in-transit items at year-end.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Reperform the in-transit schedule from the transfer register and bank statements.
Verify each in-transit item appears once: excluded from the sending account and either in transit or received, not both.
Agree the resulting cash position to the reported balance.
procedures.title: Reperform the in-transit reconciliation

procedures.exception_criteria: Counted cash less than the recorded balance; IOUs or personal items held as cash; cashier unable to explain differences.
procedures.expected_result: Cash counted agrees with the cash records; any difference is explained and supported.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate shortages with the cashier and management; quantify the loss; assess whether the pattern indicates misappropriation - without presuming it - and consider the implications for the control environment.
procedures.objective: Obtain direct evidence of the existence of cash on hand.
procedures.population: Cash on hand at the count date (tills, petty cash, undeposited receipts).
procedures.sampling_notes: Surprise count; all cash locations counted simultaneously where practicable.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Arrive unannounced and take control of all cash at each location simultaneously.
Count cash by denomination and record independently; include undeposited receipts.
Have the count acknowledged by the custodian and retain a copy of the count record.
procedures.title: Count cash on hand

procedures.exception_criteria: Unreconciled differences; IOUs included in the cash balance; shortages written off without approval.
procedures.expected_result: The count reconciles to the cash records; differences are investigated, approved and correctly treated (IOUs are not cash).
procedures.follow_up: Quantify shortages; determine whether they indicate error or misappropriation; propose adjustment where the recorded balance is overstated.
procedures.objective: Verify that counted cash reconciles to the records and differences are properly dealt with.
procedures.population: Cash count results and cash records at the count date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Not applicable - reconciliation of the count.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Reconcile the counted total to the petty cash records and cash book.
Inspect IOUs or other non-cash items found; verify they are not included in the cash balance.
Investigate and document the resolution of each difference.
procedures.title: Reconcile the count to cash records and investigate differences

procedures.exception_criteria: Counts performed by the cashier alone; announced counts; differences not followed up.
procedures.expected_result: Counts are performed by an independent person, unannounced, with differences investigated.
procedures.follow_up: Weaknesses in count discipline are control deficiencies. Increase the extent of the auditor's own physical verification.
procedures.objective: Determine whether the entity's cash count controls operate as designed.
procedures.population: Cash counts performed in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Observe at least one count; inspect records of others.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Observe an entity cash count where one is scheduled, noting independence and surprise.
Inspect count sheets and reconciliations for other counts in the period.
Note whether differences were investigated and approved.
procedures.title: Observe the entity's cash count procedures

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where outstanding items are aged or material; stale deposits in transit or long-unpresented cheques may not represent real amounts.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: The recorded cash balance may include reconciling items that no longer exist - for example deposits in transit that never arrived - so the balance includes cash that does not exist.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where the entity has automatic bank transactions outside the purchase and sales ledgers (charges, interest, direct debits).
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Bank-originated transactions such as charges, interest and direct debits may never be recorded if the reconciliation that would surface them is not reviewed.

risk_assertions.conditions: Core assertion for this risk; tested by vouching payments to independent evidence of the underlying transaction.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Payments to fictitious or improper beneficiaries are recorded as genuine business transactions that did not occur as legitimate expenditure.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where supporting documentation is weak or the account coding is unusual for the payee; tested by inspecting the accounts charged.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Improper payments may be deliberately misclassified - charged to vague expense accounts - to conceal their nature.

risk_assertions.conditions: Central to this risk; tested by matching both sides of each year-end transfer to value dates.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Transfers recorded on the receiving side before the value date, or on one side only at year-end, are recorded in the wrong period.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where in-transit amounts are material; the specific concern is the same cash existing in two accounts at once.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Cash recorded as received while still in transit is double-counted: the reported balance includes cash that does not exist in the form stated.

risk_assertions.conditions: The primary assertion for cash on hand; tested by direct physical count.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: If cash has been removed without record, the recorded balance includes cash that no longer exists.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant only where IOUs, unreconciled shortages or other non-cash items are found in the cash balance.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: IOUs or concealed shortages included in the balance overstate its realisable amount; the balance is not fully recoverable as cash.

risk_controls.explanation: Independent review is the control the factor says is missing; it is the primary detective control over bank transactions.
Prevents stale items from permanently distorting the balance - the specific failure mode of an unreviewed reconciliation.
Directly addresses the factor by establishing beneficiary legitimacy before money moves.
Dual authorisation with matched documents is the last barrier before funds leave the entity.
The transfer register is the population the auditor tests; matching both sides prevents one-sided recording.
Year-end cut-off procedures specifically address the double-counting and window-dressing risk.
Independent counts are the direct detective control over cash on hand.
Dual custody and prompt banking reduce the opportunity for removal before recording.

risk_procedures.reason: Tests whether the review control the factor says is missing actually operates.
Independent reperformance establishes whether the reported cash balance reconciles.
Aged outstanding items are where concealed differences hide; each must clear or be explained.
Direct bank confirmation provides independent evidence of the balance, bypassing the unreviewed reconciliation.
Vouching unusual payments to supporting documents is the primary occurrence test.
Full-population analysis finds anomalous beneficiaries that sampling might miss.
Directly tests the factor: whether new beneficiaries were verified before payment.
Tests whether authorisation controls operated over the payments under suspicion.
Matching both sides to value dates is the definitive cut-off test for transfers.
Bank-issued advices corroborate the transfers independently of the entity's records.
Reperformance of the in-transit position proves the cash balance is not double-counted.
Direct physical count is the primary existence test for cash on hand.
Reconciliation of the count to records identifies shortages and improper inclusions such as IOUs.
Tests whether the entity's own count controls operate, determining reliance.

risks.causes: No independent review of reconciliations; reconciliations prepared late or not at all; long-outstanding items never investigated; preparer also handles cash.
risks.description: Unrecorded bank charges, direct debits, errors, or misappropriation through the bank account are not identified because the reconciliation is not subject to independent scrutiny.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with transaction volume, the number of automatic bank transactions, and where the preparer handles cash. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists - it is a control deficiency creating detection risk, and the balance must be tested.
risks.potential_consequences: Cash balance misstated; unrecorded liabilities or expenses (bank charges, automatic payments); fraud through the bank account concealed by stale reconciling items.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Errors and irregularities in bank transactions remain undetected

risks.causes: No verification of new beneficiaries; weak payment approval; beneficiary master data uncontrolled; supporting documents fabricated or absent.
risks.description: Funds are disbursed to fictitious or improper beneficiaries, whether through falsified supporting documents, diverted supplier payments, or payments with no business purpose.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with payment volumes, electronic payment files, and weak beneficiary controls. Unusual payments are indicators to investigate; they do NOT prove that fraud has occurred.
risks.potential_consequences: Cash misappropriated; expenses overstated or misclassified to conceal the payments; duplicate payments diverted to unauthorised accounts.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Unauthorised or fraudulent payments to unfamiliar beneficiaries

risks.causes: Timing differences not properly accounted for; transfers recorded on the receiving side only; deliberate inflation of the reported cash balance.
risks.description: Transfers recorded as received before year-end but not yet dispatched (or vice versa) double-count or omit cash, overstating or understating the reported balance - whether by error or deliberate window dressing.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with the value of transfers in the cut-off window and with pressure to present a strong liquidity position. The factor creates cut-off risk to be tested; it does NOT prove the cash balance is misstated.
risks.potential_consequences: Cash overstated through double-counting in transit; misleading liquidity position presented; compensating errors conceal the true position.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Cash misstated through year-end transfer cut-off errors

risks.causes: No independent counts; single custody of cash; IOUs treated as cash; weak receipting of cash received.
risks.description: Physical cash is removed or lost without detection, and the recorded balance exceeds cash actually held.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with the volume of cash handled and the number of people with access. The absence of verification does NOT prove any shortage exists - existence must be tested directly.
risks.potential_consequences: Cash overstated; losses concealed within the balance; a weak cash control environment signalling wider control issues.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Cash on hand misappropriated or misstated

rules.name: Bank reconciliations not independently reviewed -> undetected bank errors
rules.rationale: The bank reconciliation is the key detective control over cash; without independent review, errors and irregularities go unchallenged. The rule directs the auditor to test the review control, reperform the reconciliation, vouch aged items, and obtain direct bank confirmation.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Whether bank balances are material to the financial statements.
How often reconciliations are prepared, by whom, and whether any independent review exists.
The age profile of outstanding items in the latest reconciliation.
then.note: An unreviewed reconciliation cannot be relied upon; the cash balance must be corroborated independently through reperformance, vouching of outstanding items and bank confirmation.

rules.name: Unusual payments to unfamiliar beneficiaries -> improper payment risk
rules.rationale: Payments to unfamiliar beneficiaries bypass the implicit control of a known supplier relationship. The rule directs full-population beneficiary analysis, vouching of unusual payments to supporting documents, and tracing of new beneficiaries to verification evidence.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: The volume and value of payments to new or unfamiliar beneficiaries.
How new beneficiaries are verified before the first payment.
Payment approval thresholds and whether dual authorisation is enforced.
then.note: Unusual payments are indicators to investigate, not proof of fraud. Each anomaly is vouched to independent evidence of the underlying transaction before any conclusion is drawn.

rules.name: Year-end bank transfers -> cut-off and double-counting risk
rules.rationale: Transfers in transit at year-end can be double-counted or omitted, and may be used to window-dress liquidity. The rule directs cut-off testing that matches both sides of every material transfer to bank value dates and reperforms the in-transit position.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: The value and timing of transfers in the cut-off window around the reporting date.
Whether a transfer register is maintained and both sides are recorded in the same period.
Whether material transfers are reversed shortly after year-end.
then.note: Cut-off testing is performed on both sides of each transfer: the sending account and the receiving account. A transfer confirmed on one side only is an exception, not a timing difference.

rules.name: Cash not physically verified -> existence risk for cash on hand
rules.rationale: Cash is the most portable asset; without independent physical verification, shortages accumulate undetected. The rule directs surprise physical verification by the auditor, reconciliation of the count to records, and testing of the entity's own count controls.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Whether cash on hand is material, and where cash is held.
Who has custody of cash and whether any independent counts are performed.
The volume of cash transactions and how receipts are controlled.
then.note: Existence of cash is established by direct count, not by agreement of records. IOUs and other non-cash items found in the cash balance are not cash.
